identity.canonical_product_name: Clorox Urine Remover For Stains & Odors, Ready-to-Use, 32 oz Bottle, 6/PK
identity.formulation_description: Bleach-free, hydrogen-peroxide-based ready-to-use cleaner formulated to break down urine odors and remove protein-based stains from hard and soft surfaces.
identity.package_description: 32 oz bottle, manufacturer model 31415; Grainger item 48RF66; 6 bottles per package
aliases: Clorox Urine Remover for Stains & Odors

manufacturer_product_data.description: Bleach-free cleaner for short-term messes and long-term urine stains. The manufacturer states that hydrogen peroxide breaks down odors and lifts stains on soft, absorbent surfaces and hard, porous surfaces.
recommended_uses: Concrete, pavement, sidewalks, and outdoor tile
Human soils including feces, blood, and vomit
manufacturer_product_data.uses_advised_against: Not recommended for brass, natural marble, silk, or leather upholstery.

other_official_facts.general_application: Apply directly until the stain is covered, then rinse with water or wipe with a clean damp cloth.
other_official_facts.painted_surface_instruction: Test a small area for colorfastness before use.

data.product_identifier: Clorox Urine Remover For Stains & Odors

hazard_statements: The mixture does not meet the criteria for classification.

disposal: Dispose of container in accordance with local, regional, national, and international regulations.

data.other_hazards: No hazards not otherwise classified are known.

data.trade_secret_note: The exact percentage has been withheld as a trade secret under 29 CFR 1910.1200 paragraph (i).

general_advice: If unwell, seek medical advice and show the label or SDS where possible.
Keep out of reach of children and pets.
data.eyes: Flush with water for 15 minutes. If irritation persists, call a doctor.
data.skin: Flush with cool water, wash with soap and water, and obtain medical attention if irritation persists.
data.inhalation: Move the person into fresh air.
data.ingestion: Drink a glassful of water and call a doctor or poison control center.
data.most_important_symptoms_effects: Direct eye contact may cause temporary irritation.
data.immediate_medical_attention: Provide general supportive measures and treat symptomatically; symptoms may be delayed.

suitable_extinguishing_media: Use extinguishing media appropriate for the surrounding material.
data.unsuitable_extinguishing_media: Do not use a water jet because it may spread the fire; water spray may be inefficient.
specific_hazards: Gases hazardous to health may be formed during fire.
data.firefighter_protection: Wear self-contained breathing apparatus and full protective clothing.
special_methods: Move containers from the fire area if this can be done without risk.
Use standard firefighting procedures and consider hazards of other involved materials.
No unusual fire or explosion hazards are noted.

personal_precautions: Keep unnecessary personnel away and upwind of the spill.
Do not touch damaged containers or spilled material without appropriate protection.
protective_equipment: Wear appropriate protective equipment and clothing during cleanup.
emergency_procedures: Advise local authorities if significant spills cannot be contained.
environmental_precautions: Prevent discharge into drains, waterways, lakes, streams, ponds, or public waters.
Prevent further leakage or spillage if safe to do so.
containment: Prevent entry into waterways, sewers, basements, or confined areas.
Prevent large spills from entering sewers or waterways.
cleanup: Absorb small spills with non-reactive absorbent.
Place collected material in suitable covered and labeled containers.
Contact emergency services and the supplier for advice on large spills.

safe_handling: Avoid contact with eyes, skin, or clothing.
Do not eat or drink while using the product.
storage_conditions: Keep out of reach of children and pets.

data.engineering_controls: Use good general ventilation, typically 10 air changes per hour, and match ventilation to conditions. Use enclosure or local exhaust where needed to maintain acceptable airborne levels.
data.eye_protection: Normally not required under normal use conditions; use safety glasses with side shields if splashing is likely.
data.hand_protection: Normally not required when used as directed; wear rubber gloves for prolonged use.
data.skin_body_protection: Wear appropriate chemical-resistant clothing as required by employer policy.
data.respiratory_protection: Use an approved NIOSH respirator where exposure guidelines may be exceeded, selected and supervised by a trained health and safety professional.
hygiene_measures: Wash hands before breaks and immediately after handling.
Wash before eating, drinking, or smoking.
Routinely wash work clothing and protective equipment.
Do not eat or drink while using the product.

data.reactivity: May react with strong oxidizing agents.
possibility_of_hazardous_reactions: No dangerous reaction is known under normal conditions of use.
conditions_to_avoid: Do not mix with other chemicals.

symptoms.inhalation: No adverse effects are expected during normal use; excessive intentional inhalation may irritate the respiratory tract.
symptoms.skin: Not expected to be a primary skin irritant.
symptoms.eyes: Direct contact may cause temporary irritation.
symptoms.ingestion: May cause stomach distress, nausea, or vomiting.

data.acute_toxicity: The SDS provides ingredient-level hydrogen-peroxide acute toxicity data.
data.skin_corrosion_irritation: Not expected to be a primary skin irritant.
data.serious_eye_damage_irritation: Direct eye contact may cause temporary irritation.
data.respiratory_or_skin_sensitization: Not a respiratory sensitizer; skin-sensitization data not available.
data.carcinogenicity: Product not classified. Hydrogen peroxide is ACGIH A3 and IARC Group 3.
data.reproductive_toxicity: Not expected to cause reproductive or developmental effects.

data.prepared_by: The Clorox Company; SDS text prepared by Dell Tech Laboratories Ltd.
